title: Cross-sectional STEM Imaging of the Interfacial Structure and Defects in Twisted Epitaxial MoS2-Au-MoS2 Heterostructures
content: Two-dimensional (2D) materials hold potential for creating novel heterostructures for energy and electronic devices, with metal contacts or intercalations playing a crucial role in their functionalities [1]. A comprehensive understanding of the metal-2D material interface, including its atomic structure, interfacial chemistry, and properties, is critical for optimizing performance and guiding the design of advanced, sustainable devices [2]. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is a powerful tool for atomic-scale analysis of materials. Cross-sectional STEM, in particular, is suitable for examining the atomic structure and tracking the structural evolution at the metal-2D material interfaces [2].
